```json
{"action": "refine", "reason": "Topology is correct; only 1/f noise (2-15% over) and one settling corner fail. Raising the pair's gate area (larger L1, higher gm/Id, more I1) cuts flicker noise. More tail current also improves slew for sf/-40C. A slightly larger Cc protects PM against the larger d1/d2 capacitance.", "params": {"gmid1": 18.5, "L1": 2.6, "I1": 24e-6, "Cc": 2.4e-12, "I7": 240e-6, "kRz": 1.6}, "bounds": {"L1": [2.2, 3.0], "gmid1": [16.0, 20.0], "I1": [20e-6, 40e-6], "Cc": [1.8e-12, 3.5e-12], "I7": [180e-6, 350e-6]}}
```

The new start point is aimed at noise with margin and assumes flicker noise scales roughly with 1/sqrt(gate area):

- **Flicker noise:** L1 goes from 2 to 2.6 µm, gm/Id from 17 to 18.5, and I1 from 20 to 24 µA. Together these give about 2.4× more pair gate area, which should cut 1/f noise by about 1.5×. The worst corner (266 nV/√Hz at fs/125C) would then land well under the 230 nV limit.
- **Slew:** Itail/Cc rises from about 18 V/µs to 20 V/µs, which helps the sf/-40C/1.62V settling failure (78 ns).
- **Unchanged parts:** I7 rises slightly to keep the second pole well clear as gm1 goes up. Power stays around 0.6 mW, well under the budget.
